passage:
The town library has a shelf that does not hold books. It holds seeds.
People can take small packets of vegetable or flower seeds for free. After they grow the plants, they are asked to bring back some new seeds if they can.
At first, the idea sounded strange. But many people joined. Children planted sunflowers. Grandparents grew tomatoes. Some families tried vegetables they had never eaten before.
The librarian says a seed library and a book library are not so different. Both give people something small that can grow into something larger.
A book can grow ideas in the mind. A seed can grow food or flowers in the ground. Both need time, care, and someone willing to begin.
